superseded_findings.problem: Authorization keys on the token's owner while the filesystem backend joins owner and name, and _resolve_safe_path only prevented escaping the storage root, so a token with the requester's own owner and a name of '../<victim>/secret.pdf' passed Rule A and resolved into another owner's directory.
superseded_findings.impact: The cross-user read this ticket closes stayed reachable on the default filesystem backend by moving the payload from the owner field to the name field, defeating AC2 and AC4. Cloud backends unaffected: their keys are literal.
superseded_findings.recommendation: Resolve against <root>/<owner> and refuse anything leaving it; also reject such a token in the router so the answer stays the shared 404 rather than a 500.

superseded_findings.problem: The screenshot owner was taken from execution_context.user_id, which for a global assistant or workflow is the creator (workflows/nodes/agent_node.py sets it from workflow_config.created_by), not the user running it.
superseded_findings.impact: Every MCP screenshot produced through a global assistant or workflow would be owned by someone who is not present, so Rule A denies it and the user who produced it gets a 404 on their own screenshot.
superseded_findings.recommendation: Take the owner from execution_context.user_context.id, the authenticated initiator of the request.

superseded_findings.problem: The share endpoint issues grants for both carriers (file_names entries and inline sandbox:/v1/files/<token> references) while Rule E matched only file_names, falling back to a workspace lookup that D-1 documents as unreliable on the default agent route.
superseded_findings.impact: A recipient receives a granted URL for an inline-referenced file and is still denied, so shared conversations render broken images with an error that is deliberately indistinguishable from a denial.
superseded_findings.recommendation: Derive the authorized token set from the same collector the share endpoint grants from.

superseded_findings.problem: Ability(user).can(...) sat outside the helper's try/except, and Rules B, D and E issue Postgres/Elasticsearch lookups that run before the storage try block, so a backend error escaped as a 500.
superseded_findings.impact: Breaks the documented fail-closed contract and reintroduces an existence oracle: 500 for 'exists but the lookup broke' against 404 for 'denied', which the shared 404 was built to remove.
superseded_findings.recommendation: Cover the Ability evaluation in the same try, and wrap the authorization call so anything unexpected is logged and denied with the shared 404.

superseded_findings.problem: The MCP_IMAGES_SUBDIR fallback still writes new blobs into the namespace Rule C grants to every authenticated user, while Rule C's comment claimed those blobs only predate the change and that the path decays.
superseded_findings.impact: The residual does not shrink on its own and the rule can never be safely removed, while the code comment misrepresents the actual exposure.
superseded_findings.recommendation: Log the unattributed write so the path is observable, and correct the comment, spec and design to name the real accepted exception with an exit condition.

superseded_findings.problem: The test mocks the session so first() returns the sentinel unconditionally and asserts only identity, so it passes with the workspace_id, blob_owner and blob_name predicates deleted.
superseded_findings.impact: Rule E's whole scoping check has no regression coverage; widening it to 'any blob with this name in any workspace' would ship green.
superseded_findings.recommendation: Assert the compiled statement carries the mandatory predicates, as the companion mime_type test already does.

superseded_findings.problem: The mermaid SVG is fetched with a bare fetch(file_url) that carries no auth headers and defaults to credentials: 'same-origin', unlike every api.* call which sends credentials explicitly.
superseded_findings.impact: With the endpoint now authenticated, mermaid diagrams fail with 401 wherever the API origin differs from the app origin.
superseded_findings.recommendation: Send the same credentials as the rest of the client.

finding_status.evidence: _resolve_safe_path now resolves against <root>/<owner> and refuses anything leaving it; _points_outside_owner rejects such a token in the router before any rule so the answer stays the shared 404. Verified against the old and new implementations directly: the old one resolved 'attacker' + '../victim/secret.pdf' to <root>/victim/secret.pdf and accepted it; the new one rejects it while still allowing plain names and subdirectory names such as workflows/{id}.svg. Tests #16 and #17.
The owner now comes from execution_context.user_context.id, the authenticated initiator. Pinned by test_owner_is_the_initiator_not_the_credential_owner, which fails if user_id is used.

Both halves now call collect_message_file_tokens in share_conversation_service, so the granted set and the authorized set are derived from one function. An exact-membership check also avoids the false grant a substring match would give when one token prefixes another.

The Ability evaluation moved inside the helper's try; the _authorize_file_access call is wrapped so ExtendedHTTPException propagates and anything else is logged and denied with the shared 404. Test #18 drives a RuntimeError from the share lookup and asserts 404.

The unattributed write now logs a warning, and Rule C's comment, spec.md and design A-4 state the real accepted exception with the exit condition that would allow the rule to be dropped. The residual itself is accepted, not closed.
test_find_by_blob_scopes_the_query_to_workspace_owner_and_name asserts the compiled statement carries the workspace_id, blob_owner, blob_name and mime_type predicates.
codemie-ui getMermaidFile sends credentials: 'include' and api.authHeaders(), matching every other API call. typecheck, eslint and the files store suite pass.

rationale: Final effective verdict after check round: all 7 blocking findings (CR-001..CR-007) from the initial review were resolved and independently verified in code-review-check.json. Business review was re-evaluated after the fixes - AC1, AC2 and AC4 pass, and AC3 stays partial only on the recorded D-7 deviation, which is not a regression. Standards review is clean, including the fail-closed parsing standard that CR-004 had left partial. The round-1 findings are retained under superseded_findings so the audit trail survives, and per-finding evidence lives in code-review-check.json.
